title: Onion-Marinated Lamb Shashlik
summary: Lamb leg is marinated in grated onion, garlic and warm spices, then threaded onto skewers with onion pieces and grilled over high heat until charred, served with quick-pickled red onion rings and fresh herbs.
equipment: barbecue or ridged cast-iron griddle pan

ingredients.item: boneless lamb leg (or shoulder), trimmed, cut into 4 cm cubes
fine sea salt or table salt
onion, cut into 3 cm pieces, layers separated
red onion, sliced into thin rings

steps.title: Make the marinade and add the lamb
steps.text: Mix the grated onion and its juice with the garlic, lemon juice, vinegar, oil, coriander, cumin, bay, salt and pepper in a large bowl or food bag. Add the lamb, massage it well into the marinade, then cover and refrigerate for 4-12 hours, turning once partway through. The onion juice and acidity work on the surface of the meat over this time, softening it slightly and carrying flavour deep into the cubes.

steps.title: Quick-pickle the onion rings
steps.text: About 30 minutes before serving, soak the thinly sliced red onion rings in iced water with the vinegar. This short soak takes the harsh raw bite out of the onion while keeping the rings crisp, rather than limp. Drain well before serving.

steps.title: Thread the skewers
steps.text: Lift the lamb out of the marinade and scrape off most of the clinging grated onion, as it tends to burn before the meat is done. Thread the lamb onto the skewers alternating with the onion pieces, keeping the meat pieces just touching, and discard the leftover marinade.

steps.title: Grill the shashlik
steps.text: Heat the barbecue or griddle pan over high heat until very hot, then grill the skewers for 10-12 minutes, turning every 2-3 minutes. Look for well-charred edges on the lamb and onion, and check with a probe thermometer that the centre of the thickest cube reads 63°C.

steps.title: Rest and serve
steps.text: Rest the skewers under foil for 5 minutes before serving, which allows the juices driven to the centre during grilling to redistribute through the meat. Serve with the drained pickled onion rings and a scattering of fresh dill or parsley.

tips: Scrape off the clinging grated onion before threading the lamb onto skewers — left on, it burns quickly and turns bitter before the meat is cooked.
Marinate for the full 4-12 hours if you can; the onion and acid need time to work into the lamb, and a shorter marinade gives a milder result.
Soak the red onion rings in iced water rather than serving them raw straight from the knife — this softens their sharp bite without making them limp.
Use a probe thermometer in the thickest part of the largest cube (63°C) rather than cutting into the meat to check, which lets juices escape.
Rest the skewers under foil for the full 5 minutes before serving so the juices settle back through the meat instead of running out onto the plate.
storage: Store cooked lamb in a covered container in the fridge for up to 2 days. Reheat gently until piping hot throughout (74°C) in a pan or oven; the pickled onion rings are best made fresh and eaten within a few hours. Cool leftovers in a shallow container and refrigerate within 2 hours (within 1 hour on a day above 32°C).
